opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform and winning new merchants. Up 10% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and new commerce and AI features. Down 46% YoY, from $648M a year ago, when layoff-related charges inflated the figure.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Down 54% YoY, from $131M a year ago, helped by a $55M legal-contingency benefit.

opex.name: Transaction and loan losses
opex.note: Losses on merchant loans and cash advances, and transaction losses. Up 35% YoY as more sales flowed through Shopify Payments.

follow100Note: Subscription plans bring in $27.53 of every $100 and merchant solutions $72.46 — mostly a cut of merchants' sales. Direct costs take $48.90 and running the business takes another $39.31, leaving $11.79 of operating profit per $100. Other income added just $0.29, and after a $44M equity-method loss and $32M of tax, Shopify kept $8.36 of every $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: The earnings release prints a condensed statement (operating income $241M, total other expense $38M, net income $171M); the split of that $38M into interest income, investment losses, the equity-method loss and the foreign-exchange gain comes from the detailed interim financial statements in Exhibit 99.1 of the same Form 6-K, as the release itself directs.
oneTimers: $120M of investment losses: a $79M unrealized loss on equity and other investments (partly offset by a $3M realized gain) plus a $44M loss on Shopify's equity-method investment in Flexport. Excluding equity investments, adjusted net income was $345M (non-GAAP) versus $171M GAAP net income.
A $55M benefit related to legal contingencies sits inside general and administrative expenses — G&A fell 54% YoY to $60M, but adjusted G&A (excluding the benefit) was $92M.

Stock-based compensation of $106M — a non-cash expense inside operating expenses ($70M in R&D, $23M in G&A, $10M in sales and marketing, plus $3M in cost of revenues). It is recurring, not one-off, but it is paid in shares rather than cash, so it does not reduce the $333M of free cash flow Shopify generated.

The year-ago quarter included a $1,340M impairment on the sale of Shopify's logistics businesses plus $165M of accelerated stock-based compensation and $148M of severance — so the swing from a $1,636M operating loss to a $241M profit is mostly the absence of those charges; on an adjusted basis, operating income rose from $146M to $299M.
otherDetail: Other income of $6M in total: $80M of interest income, a $3M realized gain and a $2M foreign-exchange gain, mostly offset by a $79M unrealized loss on equity and other investments. The $44M equity-method loss is the separate equityM line; the rest nets to otherIncomeM of $6M.
pngFooterNote: Back to operating profit; investment losses cut net income.

segments.name: Subscription solutions
segments.note: The monthly plans merchants pay to run their stores on Shopify. Up 27% YoY; monthly recurring revenue reached $169M.

segments.name: Merchant solutions
segments.note: Mostly payment processing (Shopify Payments) — a cut of the sales flowing through merchants' stores — plus shipping and other merchant services. Up 19% YoY and 72% of all revenue.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 21% to $2.05B as GMV grew 22% to $67.2B — 25% after adjusting for the sale of the logistics businesses. Subscription revenue grew 27% to $563M on more merchants and higher plan prices, with monthly recurring revenue up 25% to $169M, while merchant solutions rose 19% to $1.48B as Shopify Payments processed 61% of GMV.
takeaways.title: Growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: Operating income was $241M (12% margin) versus a $1,636M loss a year ago — but that loss included a $1,340M charge for selling the logistics businesses. On an adjusted basis, operating income doubled to $299M from $146M, and gross margin widened to 51.1% from 49.3% as the dilutive logistics business exited. Free cash flow more than tripled to $333M, a 16% margin versus 6% a year ago.
takeaways.title: Back in operating profit — with an asterisk

takeaways.text: Net income was $171M, but $120M of investment losses cut into it: a $79M unrealized loss on equity investments (partly offset by a $3M realized gain) plus a $44M loss on the Flexport stake. Excluding equity investments, adjusted net income was $345M — nearly double the $178M a year ago.
takeaways.title: Investment losses trimmed the bottom line

verdict: Shopify grew revenue 21% to $2.0B and returned to a $241M operating profit — but $120M of investment losses, including a $44M loss on its Flexport stake, held net income to $171M.
